children: Copper rose on Friday and was on track for its first weekly gain in seven weeks, as equities found their footing after a bruising AI-driven selloff.
The benchmark three-month copper on the London Metals Exchange
climbed 3.76% to $12,318 a metric ton as of 0330 GMT. It is up more than 1% for the week so far.
The most-active copper contract (SCFv1) on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SCFv1) jumped 4.74% to 92,980 yuan  ($13,961.59) a ton, on track to end the week up nearly 1%.
The Shanghai contract jumped as much as 5.22% this morning, the strongest gain since end-January.
The rise in copper, a key metal for electrification and AI data centres, came as global equity markets stabilised after a selloff in AI-related stocks this month.
Wall Street was closed for the Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday, while Asian shares rose and Nasdaq futures
advanced more than 2%.

Also supporting sentiment, data showed that profits at China's industrial firms rose 20.1% year-on-year in October, the fastest pace in five months. Growth was uneven across sectors, with particularly strong earnings in electronics and nonferrous metals industries.

However, copper faces some pressure from improved supply. Copper stocks monitored by the LME (MCUSTX-TOTAL) have risen since mid-October and the discount of LME cash copper to the  three-month contract, or contango, has persisted.
High premiums for copper in China are drawing units from stocks ahead of expected US tariffs, which are expected to ease extreme supply tightness in China, the biggest consumer market for copper.

The Yangshan premium (SMM-CUYP-CN), a gauge of China's appetite for imported copper was at $320 a ton as of Thursday, and the domestic premium (SMM-CU-PND) was at 2,300 yuan. Both premiums had tumbled from their records set a few days ago but remained elevated.
A near-term contango in SHFE contracts, however, remained. The most-active January contract was still at a discount of 2,310 yuan a ton to the December contract as of 0330 GMT.
Among other LME metals, aluminium
rose 1.42%, zinc
gained 1.94%, lead
edged up 0.24%, nickel
added 0.66% and tin
surged 4.50%.
Shanghai aluminium (SAFv1) gained 1.83%, zinc (SZNv1) rose 2.98%, lead (SPBv1) climbed 1.58%, nickel (SNIv1) advanced 3.41% and tin (SSNv1) jumped 5.29%.
($1 = 6.6597 Chinese yuan renminbi)
